# teltonika_rms_task_group_task (Resource)

**State-only helper resource.** Declares a single task definition (name, order, type, timeout, stop-on-failure, data) so it can be referenced from one or more `teltonika_rms_task_group` resources through the group's `tasks` attribute. 

This resource performs **no RMS API calls** on any lifecycle event — Create/Read/Update/Delete just move the plan into state. RMS creates and destroys tasks as a side effect of the group's POST/PUT (`POST /devices/tasks/groups`), so a task record only makes sense when it is spliced into a group's `tasks` list. The task-group resource is what actually talks to RMS.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# teltonika_rms_task_group_task is a state-only helper — it never talks to RMS by itself.
# Its purpose is to give a task definition a stable, named handle you can splice into one
# or more `teltonika_rms_task_group` resources.

resource "teltonika_rms_task_group_task" "reboot" {
  name            = "Reboot device"
  order           = 1
  type            = "command"
  timeout         = 30
  stop_on_failure = true

  data = {
    command = "reboot"
  }
}

# Reference it from a task group — the resource is treated as an object with matching
# attributes, so it plugs straight into the group's `tasks` list.
resource "teltonika_rms_task_group" "reboot_only" {
  name  = "Reboot only"
  tasks = [teltonika_rms_task_group_task.reboot]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `data` (Attributes) Type-specific payload sent to the device. Only the fields matching `type` are used; the rest are ignored server-side. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data))
- `name` (String) Task name as displayed in the RMS UI.
- `order` (Number) Position of the task inside the group. RMS uses this to order execution; must be >= 0.
- `stop_on_failure` (Boolean) If true, a failure aborts the remaining tasks in the group.
- `timeout` (Number) Maximum runtime of the task in seconds. Must be between 1 and 300.
- `type` (String) Task type. One of `command`, `upload_file`, `download_file`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable client-side identifier derived from `name` + `order`.

<a id="nestedatt--data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data`

Optional:

- `acceptable_codes` (List of Number) Exit codes that should NOT be treated as failure. Optional; used only when `type = command`.
- `command` (String) Shell command to execute. Required when `type = command`.
- `file` (String) Absolute path on the device of the file to fetch. Required when `type = download_file`.
- `file_id` (Number) Id of the file to push to the device. Required when `type = upload_file`.
- `target_path` (String) Absolute path on the device where the file will be written. Required when `type = upload_file`.
